New formula and epithet renderings for iliad-046 (8.1–96), in the table format of conventions.md. Reused wherever the table or a published part already had the line: 8.3b (iliad-034, "on the topmost peak of many-ridged Olympus"), 8.5–6 (the speech-opening in iliad-044, with "all gods and all goddesses" for the addressees), 8.28 (iliad-042, extended by the participle clause that follows the ano teleia), 8.31 (the Odyssey's wording, the commas absent from the Greek here but the English unchanged), 8.45b–46 (iliad-034, the whole unit identical), 8.58 (iliad-015, 2.809–810), 8.60–62, 8.63 and 8.64–65 (iliad-025, whole units; 8.60 differs from iliad-025's unit only by a comma in the Greek), 8.66 (Odyssey 9.56), 8.71a (iliad-017's half-line wording), 8.82b (iliad-019 / iliad-044) and 8.93 (iliad-008 / the table's 5.203 row). 8.59b: the whole unit πολὺς δ’ ὀρυμαγδὸς ὀρώρει. is identical to the unit in iliad-015 and in odyssey-115 ("and a great din had risen." / "and a great din rose."), as the validator requires; the longer unit at 8.62b–63 keeps iliad-025's "had sprung up" / "went up", so the same half-line has two English wordings in the Iliad, a pre-existing inconsistency. Reviewer: left as it is, because the validator binds each of the two units to its published English (iliad-015 / odyssey-115 for 8.59b, iliad-025 for 8.62b–63) and no published part may be touched here; the conventions row for 2.810 ("had sprung up" / "went up") disagrees with the shipped iliad-015, which is the owner's to harmonise. Both notes say so. Units 8.81–82 and 8.83–84 are one unit (8.81–84), since 8.82 ends with no stop. 8.38 (τὴν δ’ ἐπιμειδήσας προσέφη νεφεληγερέτα Ζεύς) is built from the 4.356 and 22.371 rows.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ἠὼς μὲν κροκόπεπλος ἐκίδνατο πᾶσαν ἐπ’ αἶαν (8.1, whole-line dawn-formula; κροκόπεπλος is the stock epithet of Dawn) | "Dawn, saffron-robed, for her part, was spreading herself over all the earth," | "Dawn in her saffron robe was spreading over all the earth," | "yellow-robed", "in her saffron gown", "the saffron-cloaked dawn"; μέν answered by δέ in 8.2 is "for her part"; ἐκίδνατο "was spreading", imperfect middle of κίδνημι |
| ἀγορὴν ποιήσατο (8.2) | "made an assembly" | "held an assembly" | "called a council", "summoned the gods"; ἀγορή keeps "assembly" (2.788, 17.52) and the middle ποιέομαι "make for oneself" gives the idiom "held" in `i` |
| αὐτὸς δέ σφ’ ἀγόρευε (8.4) | "and he himself declared to them" | "he himself declared to them" | "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη), "spoke out" (turned down at 1.384); follows the table's ἀγορεύω "declare" for a public pronouncement; the same verb at 8.29 (μάλα γὰρ κρατερῶς ἀγόρευσεν, of the same speech) is "declared" too |
| μήτέ τις οὖν θήλεια θεὸς τό γε μήτέ τις ἄρσην πειράτω (8.7–8) | "And let no female god, then, in this at least, nor any male, try" | "And let no goddess, then, nor any god either, at least in this, try" | "no goddess or god", "let none of the gods"; θήλεια θεός keeps the plain "female god" in `l`, ἄρσην "male"; τό γε "in this at least" |
| διακέρσαι ἐμὸν ἔπος (8.8) | "to cut across my word" | "to thwart my word" | "to break my word" (ambiguous: breaking a promise), "to override", "to defy" (each adds a motive); διακείρω "cut through", ἔπος "word" |
| αἰνεῖτ’ (8.9) | "approve" | "approve it" | "applaud" (the first draft), "praise", "assent"; αἰνέω is "approve" in the Odyssey (αἰνήσουσιν, odyssey-080; αἰνεῖτον, odyssey-088), in both layers |
| ὃν δ’ ἂν ἐγὼν ἀπάνευθε θεῶν ἐθέλοντα νοήσω ἐλθόντ’ ἢ Τρώεσσιν ἀρηγέμεν ἢ Δαναοῖσι (8.10–11) | "And whomever I shall perceive, apart from the gods, willing having gone to help either the Trojans or the Danaans" | "Whichever god I perceive going of his own will, apart from the gods, to help either the Trojans or the Danaans" | "whoever I see", "who is willing to go", "wishing to help"; νοέω "perceive" (the table's ὀξὺ νόησε "sharply noticed"), ἀρήγω "help" (4.7), ἐθέλω "wish, be willing"; Δαναοί "Danaans" per the Iliad's departure |

| ἄκρην κὰκ κορυφήν, ὅθι τε πρῶται τρίχες ἵππων κρανίῳ ἐμπεφύασι, μάλιστα δὲ καίριόν ἐστιν (8.83–84) | "on the topmost crown, where the first hairs of horses grow on the skull, and where it is most deadly." | "on the very top of its head, where the first hairs of horses grow on the skull, and where a wound is most deadly." | "forelock" (πρῶται τρίχες need not be only the forelock), "the vital spot", "fatal"; καίριος "deadly, at the vital spot", the note says so |
| ἀλγήσας δ’ ἀνέπαλτο, βέλος δ’ εἰς ἐγκέφαλον δῦ (8.85) | "and in pain it leapt up, and the missile into the brain sank," | "In pain it leapt up, and the arrow sank into its brain," | "quivered", "reared" (neither is in the Greek); βέλος "missile" in `l` and "arrow" in `i`, as the arrow of 8.81; ἀναπάλλομαι "leap up", ἐγκέφαλος "brain" per the table |
| σὺν δ’ ἵππους ἐτάραξε κυλινδόμενος περὶ χαλκῷ (8.86) | "and the horses it threw into confusion, rolling about the bronze." | "and, writhing round the bronze point, it threw the horses into confusion." | "scattered", "panicked", "drove wild"; ταράσσω "throw into confusion", κυλίνδομαι "roll about"; "bronze" is the arrow-point, as the table's "bronze" for χαλκός |
| ἵπποιο παρηορίας ἀπέταμνε φασγάνῳ ἀΐσσων (8.87–88) | "the traces of the horse with his sword, darting at them" | "the horse’s traces, darting at them with his sword" | "reins" (ἡνία), "harness", "yoke-straps" (each fixes a piece of gear the word does not); παρηορίαι "traces", the note says the exact gear is not certain; ἀΐσσω "dart" per the table (ἠΐχθη, 3.367); φάσγανον "sword" |
| ἀν’ ἰωχμὸν θρασὺν ἡνίοχον φορέοντες Ἕκτορα (8.89–90) | "came through the press of the fight, bearing a bold charioteer, Hector;" | "came through the press of the fight, carrying their bold charioteer, Hector;" | "through the din" (ὀρυμαγδός), "the rout", "the onset"; ἰωχμός is rare, "press of the fight" is a guess marked in the note; ἡνίοχος "charioteer" (5.231) |
| καί νύ κεν ἔνθ’ ὁ γέρων ἀπὸ θυμὸν ὄλεσσεν εἰ μὴ ἄρ’ ὀξὺ νόησε βοὴν ἀγαθὸς Διομήδης (8.90–91) | "and now there the old man would have lost his life, if Diomedes, good at the war-cry, had not sharply noticed it;" | "And now there the old man would have lost his life, had not Diomedes, good at the war-cry, been quick to notice;" | "heart" for θυμόν (the table's θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ "lose his life"), "perceived at once"; ὀξὺ νόησε as the table's 5.680 (the table's "sharply noticed" / "been quick to notice"), βοὴν ἀγαθὸς Διομήδης per the table |
| σμερδαλέον δ’ ἐβόησεν ἐποτρύνων Ὀδυσῆα (8.92, whole-line speech introduction) | "and terribly he shouted, urging on Odysseus:" | "and he shouted terribly, urging on Odysseus:" | "dreadfully" (the first draft; the table has σμερδαλέα ἰάχων "terribly crying out" at 5.302 and "shouting dreadfully" is among its avoided renderings), "with a fearful cry", "called out"; σμερδαλέος as an adverb is "terribly", βοάω "shout", ὀτρύνω "urge on" (4.73) |
| πῇ φεύγεις μετὰ νῶτα βαλὼν κακὸς ὣς ἐν ὁμίλῳ (8.94) | "where do you flee, having turned your back, like a base man in the throng?" | "where are you fleeing, with your back turned, like a base man in the throng?" | "like a coward" (the table's κακὸς ὣς "like a base man", 6.443), "in the crowd", "in the melee"; ὅμιλος "throng" |
| μή τίς τοι φεύγοντι μεταφρένῳ ἐν δόρυ πήξῃ (8.95) | "lest someone, as you flee, fix a spear in your back;" | "lest someone fix a spear in your back as you flee;" | "plant", "drive", "thrust"; πήγνυμι "fix" per the table's ἐν δόρυ πῆξεν (5.40) |
